extraction.name: SeamlessM4T
extraction.description: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation—a single model that supports speech-to-speech translation, speech-to-text translation, text-to-speech translation, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages. Includes the SeamlessAlign dataset of automatically aligned speech translations.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: Created a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations (SeamlessAlign) totaling 470,000 hours. Used 1 million hours of open speech audio data for self-supervised speech representations. Combined a filtered subset of SeamlessAlign with human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data, totaling 406,000 hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some samples from the evaluation data (CVSS) were missing in 8 out of 21 languages: Catalan, German, Estonian, French, Italian, Mongolian, Persian, and Portuguese.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data. Text data from the same dataset deployed in NLLB.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Parallel data mining using a margin criterion with the Stopes data processing library. Speech mining performed using SONAR embeddings to identify translation pairs with optimal segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio: Deduplicated URLs, downloaded, resampled at 16KHz, filtered non-speech data with audio event detection (AED), segmented using Voice Activity Detection (VAD) and over-segmentation. Text: Same cleaning and filtering steps as NLLB run with Stopes library. Training data: Removed special tokens, length filtering (max 100 sub-words, skewed ratio), toxicity filter (imbalance threshold 1), length filter (0.1-50s audio, max 250 sub-words text), removed pairs with >20% emojis, >50% punctuations, or >50% spaces.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo-labeling of ASR data with a multilingual T2TT model (NLLB-200-3.3B). Human-labeled data from existing sources (CoVoST, mTEDx, etc.). Human evaluation used XSTS and MOS protocols with 3-5 annotators per item.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human error analysis of detected toxicity items to determine true positives vs false positives. Calibration set used to reduce language-level annotator biases in evaluation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated from the training data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Augmenting world-readiness by lowering barriers in cross-lingual communication. Supports inclusion and accessibility for those lacking reading/writing skills or with visual impairments. Helps circumvent multiscript conundrums for languages with script variance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: SeamlessM4T overgeneralizes to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (average preference of ~10%). Lack of robustness when varying gender by ~3%. Masculine representation is predominant in the analyzed datasets. Added toxicity varies by language and demographic axis (e.g., body type, nonce, sexual orientation).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Word list-based toxicity detection tends to over-detect terms toxic only in specific contexts and relies on precise tokenization (difficult for non-segmenting/agglutinative languages). ASR before lexical matching adds error (false negatives). Noun lists for gender imbalance detection have limitations regarding inclusive plural forms and generalizability. ASR performance may vary based on gender, race, accent, or language. Translating slang or proper nouns may be inconsistent. Not intended for long-form translation or domain-specific inputs (medical/legal).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Research in speech and text translation. ASR, S2ST, S2TT, T2ST, T2TT, TTS.
